gaps.sentence: ___ keep the audience engaged, the lecturer used live demonstrations.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'In order to + infinitive' states the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: We took the coast road ___ the motorway to enjoy the views.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + noun' marks the rejected alternative.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ her age, she still runs marathons.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun (her age); the conjunctions would need a clause.

gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The scheme is costly; on the ___ hand, it would create hundreds of jobs.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' balances a drawback against an advantage.

gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: We went for a long walk ___ it was drizzling.
gaps.explanation: Only the conjunction 'even though' can introduce the finite clause 'it was drizzling'.
